title: Mark 15:42–47
context: As evening approaches on the day before the Sabbath, Joseph of Arimathea, a respected council member who was waiting for God’s kingdom, boldly asks Pilate for Jesus’ body. Pilate confirms Jesus is dead, then grants the body. Joseph wraps it in linen, lays it in a rock tomb, and rolls a stone across the entrance, while two of the women watch. The burial confirms that Jesus truly died and sets up the empty tomb. Both traditions read this passage in essentially the same way.

verses.text: When evening had now come, because it was the Preparation Day, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
verses.arminianNotes: Evening was coming on the Preparation Day, the day before the Sabbath, so burial had to be quick (Deuteronomy 21:22–23). Arminian readers note the time pressure.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the same. This verse is shared narrative ground.

verses.text: Joseph of Arimathaea, a prominent council member who also himself was looking for God’s Kingdom, came. He boldly went in to Pilate, and asked for Jesus’ body.
verses.arminianNotes: Joseph, a respected council member who was waiting for God’s kingdom, boldly asks for the body. Arminian readers see a man stepping out in courage at real risk.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God raising up an unexpected servant. Both traditions honor Joseph’s courage.

verses.text: Pilate was surprised to hear that he was already dead; and summoning the centurion, he asked him whether he had been dead long.
verses.arminianNotes: Pilate is surprised that Jesus is already dead and checks with the centurion. Arminian readers note that this confirms Jesus truly died.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers make the same point, which counters any claim that Jesus only fainted. Both traditions treat the reality of his death as essential.

verses.text: When he found out from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
verses.arminianNotes: Pilate grants the body to Joseph. Arminian readers note the official confirmation of the death.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the same. This verse is shared ground.

verses.text: He bought a linen cloth, and taking him down, wound him in the linen cloth and laid him in a tomb which had been cut out of a rock. He rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
verses.arminianNotes: Joseph wraps the body in linen, lays it in a rock-cut tomb, and rolls a stone over the entrance. Arminian readers see a respectful burial that also makes the tomb easy to identify.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the same, often linking it to Isaiah 53:9 (with the rich in his death). Both traditions see the burial as part of the gospel itself (1 Corinthians 15:3–4).

verses.text: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses, saw where he was laid.
verses.arminianNotes: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses see where he is laid. Arminian readers note that they are witnesses who know the right tomb.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers make the same point. Both traditions see their witness preparing for the resurrection account.
